text: Councilmember/Business Executive

Tustin is my home. My wife Cheryl and I have raised our two daughters here and watched them thrive in this wonderful city. Over the past twenty years, I have come to deeply value the small-town character and quality of life that makes Tustin so very special. My background as a business executive and entrepreneur, along with my MBA from Chapman University, has shaped how I approach public service: practical, honest, accountable, and focused on results that matter most to our residents.

Four years ago, I asked the good people of Tustin for the opportunity to serve with three clear priorities: public safety as job number one, economic vitality paired with fiscal responsibility, as well as honest, transparent government. As the city’s current Mayor Pro Tem, and with your support, I have delivered on every one of them.

On public safety, police funding and officer staffing have increased, technology and equipment upgraded, and school safety strengthened. The results are clear – total crime has fallen 46 percent over the past four years. I am proud of this work and have earned the endorsements of the Tustin Police Officers Association, the Tustin Police Support Services Association, the Orange County Sheriff, and the Orange County Firefighters Association Local 3631 because they know I will continue fighting to keep our neighborhoods and schools safe.

On economic vitality and fiscal responsibility, I have supported and delivered balanced city budgets every year. Voted to advance smart, thoughtful development that grows revenue while preserving Tustin’s unique small-town character. I have also kept city fees and taxes low, reduced unnecessary regulations, accelerated our city pension paydown to retire this debt early, and increased investments in public parks, roads, traffic relief, and essential infrastructure. These steps protect affordability and ensure we can fund the critical services and quality of life measures residents depend on and enjoy.

On transparency, I have insisted on open financial disclosures, public budget workshops, and meaningful community engagement so residents can see and have a say in how their hard earned tax dollars are being spent. These same priorities continue to guide my work. With proven results and principled leadership, I will keep working tirelessly to ensure Tustin remains a safe, strong, and prosperous place for our families and the generations to follow.
I respectfully ask for your vote to continue serving the great city of Tustin. Learn more at www.rayfortustin.com.

text: Assistant Professor

My name is Dr. Thomas James “TJ” Reed. I’m running for Tustin City Council District 3 because Tustin shaped who I am, and I’m committed to helping shape its future. I want future generations to experience the same quality of life I was fortunate to have growing up and preserve what makes Tustin special.
Tustin is home. My desire to make a difference started at a young age, when I served as President at Arroyo Elementary School and ASB President at Foothill High School.

My campaign is built on three pillars: community, integrity, and service. I believe in celebrating the diversity that makes Tustin strong, leading with integrity and accountability, and putting the needs of our residents first in decisions.

I choose to personally fund my campaign rather than accept outside donations. This grassroots effort reflects my commitment to making decisions based on what’s best for Tustin residents and ensuring the community's voice remains at the center of local government.

I’ve spent my life learning how to serve others in public service. I earned a Bachelor’s in Communication from Pepperdine University, a Master’s in Public Administration from California State University, Long Beach, and a PhD in Leadership and Organizational Consulting from the University of San Diego. I completed leadership and governance programs through George Washington University and Harvard University.

I served on the Del Rey Neighborhood Council as Director of Area E and was appointed to the Del Rey Neighborhood Council Land Use and Planning Committee, where I worked with residents to address local priorities and strengthen community engagement.

Presently, I serve as an Assistant Professor at California State University, Long Beach, where I’m appointed to the President's Commission on Economic and Workforce Development. I’m an Adjunct Professor at Vermont Law and Graduate School and the National Judicial College, and trainer at University of San Diego’s Center for Restorative Justice.
One lesson I tell my students is: “We are the leaders we have been waiting for.” I’ll lead with service and integrity, pursuing policies that do the greatest good for the greatest number of people.

I advocate for preserving the safety of our community, uplifting local businesses, strengthening the Tustin Unified School District, supporting first responders, ensuring economic responsibility, addressing public health and environmental concerns, promoting transparency and accountability within local government, valuing community input in development decisions to fit the needs and values of our residents, and preserving Tustin as a community where families live, work, shop, and thrive for generations.
An elder in my family's Native American Tribe, the Oneida Nation of Wisconsin, gave me a name meaning, "He is a Good Man." Every day, I strive to live up to my name.
Deep roots, strong future. Tustin, together we rise.
